current_content_summary: Defines the core sub-distribution API: type 'a distr, mass/mu/mu1 (mu1 is the per-point probability, mu the event probability), mk/isdistr for building a distr from a mass function, support/\in/\notin, weight, is_lossless/is_full/is_uniform/is_funiform, and a long block of general lemmas (mu_le, mu_eq, mu_or/mu_and, mu_split, mu_not, mu_has_le, mu_mem*, mu1_le_eq* including r2026.02's mu1_le_eq_mu1). Several named sub-theories build concrete distributions on top: MRat (drat, rational/count-based distribution over a list), MUnit (dunit, point mass), MUniform (duniform), MFinite (abstract theory: dunifin over any FinType), MIntUniform (drange). Also defines p_max/mode (the most-likely-outcome probability/value) and dlet/mlet (monadic bind for distributions).

import_repair_note: Verified against the mined commit history: Distr has had NO symbol removed in the tracked window (r2022.04 onward) -- across six releases with symbol activity it only ever gained names (291 + 79 + 10 + 2 + 3). This is a useful negative -- an unknown-symbol failure naming a Distr name is a missing `require`, a name that did not exist yet, or a rename inside a clone. It is NOT a symbol that moved to another theory, so do not go looking for a destination to add. Distr is also not in AllCore's export closure (AllCore exports only Core, Int, Real, Xint and Ring.IntID), so `require import AllCore.` alone never provides `distr`, `mu`, `dunifin` or the sampling lemmas. Where names DO appear to have changed, look for a clone rather than a move: DBool's `dbool` / `dbool1E` are a renamed clone of Distr.MFinite's `dunifin` / `dunifinE` (see the DBool note), so the same distribution is reachable under two names depending on which theory the proof required.
